pr_title: [become] Fix Solaris regression caused by macOS tempdir perms fallback, and add Solaris fallback using its chmod syntax
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY

See the individual commit messages for more detail.
Effectively, there's a regression currently where we try to run the macOS chmod syntax on Solaris and chmod exits with return code 5, which we take to mean "authentication failure" since sshpass returns 5 in that case. Work around this by catching AnsibleAuthenticationFailure for now. A future rewrite of this logic will eliminate the need for this.

Also add an actual fallback for solaris, because newer solaris no longer ships setfacl (and even on solaris that does, it could fail on some filesystems). This fixes #74282.

##### ISSUE TYPE

- Bugfix Pull Request
- Test Pull Request

action

issue_context.title: setfacl: not found while trying to use ansible.builtin.su in Solaris 11.4 SRU 30
issue_context.body:
### Summary

I tried to use module **ansible.builtin.su** in a playbook to execute some commands with non-privileged account but failed to do so because playbook execution fails with **setfacl: not found** error. Digging in Oracle Solaris documentation, I found setfacl command has been removed from version 11.4.

Here:

https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E88353_01/html/E37839/setfacl-1.html

setfacl(1)
Name
getfacl, setfacl - display or modify the Access Control List (ACL) for files

Description
In Oracle Solaris 11.3 and earlier releases, the getfacl and setfacl commands were used to view and change POSIX-draft Access Control Lists (ACLs) on UFS filesystems.

**These commands are no longer included in Oracle Solaris 11.4 and later releases. Instead of getfacl, you can use the -v or -V options to the ls(1) command to list an ACL. Instead of setfacl, you can use the -A option to the chmod(1) command to change an ACL**.

### Issue Type

Bug Report

### Component Name

ansible.builtin.su

### Ansible Version

```console
$ ansible --version
ansible 2.10.8
```


### Configuration

```console
$ ansible-config dump --only-changed
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT(/etc/ansible/ansible.cfg) = 20
```


### OS / Environment

Source OS: Ubuntu 20.04.2 LTS (Focal Fossa) on top of WSL.
Target OS: Oracle Solaris 11.4.30.0.85.3

### Steps to Reproduce

<!--- Paste example playbooks or commands between quotes below -->
```yaml (paste below)
---
- hosts: devserver
  gather_facts: false
  vars:
    ansible_su_exe: su
    ansible_su_user: app_id

  become: yes
  become_method: su
  tasks:
    - name: Test
      ansible.builtin.command:
        argv:
          -whoami
```


### Expected Results

Run the command as non-priviliged account

### Actual Results

```console
<hostname> (127, b'', b'/bin/sh: setfacl: not found [No such file of directory]\n')
<hostname> Failed to connect to the host via ssh: /bin/sh: setfacl: not found [Not such file or directory]
```

I agree to follow the Ansible Code of Conduct
